title: Rate and speed: d = s × t
subject: math

items.prompt: A bus travels at 60 km/h. How far has it really travelled after half an hour?
items.misconceptionCode: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.

items.prompt: What does a speed of 60 km/h mean?
items.answer: The bus covers 60 km in every hour
choices: The bus covers 60 km in every hour
The bus has covered 60 km in total
The bus covers 60 km in every minute

items.prompt: A bus travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. How far does it go? Show the working.
items.answer: 150 km: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

items.prompt: A cyclist rides at 15 km/h for 4 hours. How far does she ride?
items.answer: 60 km: distance = speed × time, so 15 × 4 = 60 km.

items.prompt: Which working finds the distance travelled at 50 km/h for 3 hours?
Explain in one sentence why 60 km/h on its own is not a distance.
items.answer: Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60.
